baseline.name: Erase duplicate entries one at a time
baseline.approach: On finding a duplicate in a sorted array, shift the remaining suffix left.

why: A write cursor copies each new unique value once instead of shifting a suffix after every removal.
quantitative_comparison: For nonempty input the archive scans exactly n-1 following values; repeated deletion can perform a quadratic number of element moves. This is a work/growth comparison, not a measured speedup.
tradeoffs: Both approaches mutate the input and require sorted order. The archive leaves the unused suffix unspecified and has the same growth rate as other standard linear compaction methods.
evidence_basis: Source inspection of the slow/fast loops and the stated repeated-shift baseline; no paired timing.
